intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GABRB1 gene (137190) on chromosome 4p12.

checks.claim: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the GABRB1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Since the LGS and IS patients were heterozygous for the de novo GABRB3 and GABRB1 mutations, we also studied α1β1,3γ2L receptors containing these mutations in the in vitro het expression condition.
checks.explanation: The paper says the patient was heterozygous for a de novo GABRB1 mutation and that the mutation impaired receptor function. It does not use the name DEE45 and only proposes GABRB1 as a candidate epilepsy gene, so it does not establish causation.

checks.claim: The GABRB1 gene is located on chromosome 4p12.
checks.evidence_quote: four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1
checks.explanation: The paper mentions GABRB1. The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature, although the paper itself does not state it.

paragraphs.text: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-45 (DEE45) is a seizure disorder with onset in infancy. Reported patients have had infantile spasms or epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures. One reported patient also had severe to profound developmental impairment and hypotonia.

checks.claim: DEE45 is a seizure disorder with onset in infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: The syndrome of EIMFS was defined by (1) focal seizures with observed clinical and/or electrical migration between hemispheres and (2) seizure onset before age 6 months.
checks.explanation: GABRB1 patient had EIMFS with onset at 4 months.

checks.claim: Reported patients with DEE45 have had infantile spasms.
checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: The GABRB1 patient had infantile spasms.

checks.claim: Reported patients with DEE45 have had epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified 2 individuals with pathogenic variants in GABA receptor subunit-encoding genes not previously associated with EIMFS, but reported in association with other developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: one case each for GABRA1 and GABRB1.
checks.explanation: GABRB1 patient had EIMFS.

checks.claim: One reported patient with DEE45 had severe to profound developmental impairment.
checks.explanation: Table column 'Profound-severe Impairment' = 1 for the GABRB1 patient.

paragraphs.text: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) screened for de novo mutations in patients with 2 classic epileptic encephalopathies, infantile spasms (n = 149) and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (n = 115). One of the patients carried a de novo mutation in the GABRB1 gene. Janve et al. (2016) later identified this patient as having infantile spasms.

checks.claim: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) screened for de novo mutations in patients with infantile spasms (n = 149) and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (n = 115).
checks.evidence_quote: Here we report a screen for de novo mutations in patients with two classical epileptic encephalopathies: infantile spasms (n = 149) and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome (n = 115).
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: One patient in the Epi4K Consortium cohort carried a de novo mutation in the GABRB1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: we draw attention to the six mutations that all affect subunits of the gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ionotropic receptor (four in GABRB3, and one each in GABRA1 and GABRB1)
checks.explanation: One GABRB1 de novo mutation is reported.

checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: The paper says the Epi4K patient carrying the GABRB1 mutation had infantile spasms.

paragraphs.text: Burgess et al. (2019) studied a cohort of patients with epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (EIMFS). One of them (patient 63) had a de novo GABRB1 variant. Seizures began at 4 months of age with focal seizures. The patient was last reported at 2 years of age and had profound to severe developmental impairment and hypotonia. Burgess et al. (2019) noted that this finding expanded the phenotypic spectrum of GABA receptor subunit genes, including GABRB1, to include EIMFS. They emphasized a role for GABA-related mechanisms in EIMFS.

paragraphs.text: The heterozygous GABRB1 mutations in patients with DEE45 occurred de novo, as reported by Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013), Janve et al. (2016), and Burgess et al. (2019). This is consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.explanation: GABRB1 is described as an autosomal dominant gene.

paragraphs.text: Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013) performed exome sequencing on 264 trios in which the child had infantile spasms or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. They found de novo mutations in GABA-A receptor subunit genes in 6 patients: 4 in GABRB3 and 1 each in GABRA1 and GABRB1. The GABRB1 mutation was confirmed by Sanger sequencing and was absent from both parents. The authors suggested that individual rare mutations in different genes may converge on shared pathways. They also found significant genetic heterogeneity underlying infantile spasms and Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, and concluded that it may be difficult to predict the responsible gene from the clinical presentation.

checks.evidence_quote: We sequenced the exomes of 264 probands, and their parents, and confirmed 329 de novo mutations.
checks.explanation: The 264 trios had IS or LGS.

paragraphs.text: Janve et al. (2016) studied the de novo heterozygous GABRB1 mutation phe246-to-ser (F246S) in the patient with infantile spasms who was originally reported by Epi4K Consortium et al. (2013). In HEK293T cells, the mutation caused only a minor reduction (about 25%) in GABA-evoked peak current in the homozygous expression condition and no change in the heterozygous condition. However, it slowed current deactivation and increased single-channel mean open time and burst duration. Receptors containing the mutant subunit opened spontaneously, with a 4-fold increase in spontaneous open probability and increased holding currents. Surface levels of the mutant beta-1 subunit were slightly reduced, whereas total levels were unchanged.

checks.evidence_quote: Additionally one IS patient had a mutation in the GABAA receptor β1 subunit gene (GABRB1(F246S)).
checks.explanation: The paper names the F246S mutation and states elsewhere that it was de novo and heterozygous.

checks.evidence_quote: A recent study by the Epi4K Consortium and Epilepsy Phenome/Genome project (EPGP) identified four novel de novo mutations in the GABAA receptor β3 subunit gene
checks.explanation: The next sentence adds that one IS patient in that Epi4K study had GABRB1(F246S).

checks.explanation: The paper reports no change in the het condition.

checks.explanation: The paper reports a 4-fold increase in spontaneous open probability.

checks.claim: Receptors containing the GABRB1 F246S mutant subunit had increased holding currents.
checks.evidence_quote: Both LGS-associated GABRB3(E180G) and IS-associated GABRB1(F246S) mutations significantly increased (~5 fold) holding currents

checks.explanation: Surface levels of the mutant subunit were slightly reduced.

checks.evidence_quote: Reduced surface β1(F246S) levels without a reduction in the total levels
checks.explanation: Total levels of the mutant subunit were unchanged.

paragraphs.text: In a cohort of 135 patients with EIMFS, Burgess et al. (2019) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a de novo heterozygous missense variant in the GABRB1 gene in 1 patient. The variant (Chr4:47405633T-C) results in an ile247-to-thr (I247T) substitution. It was absent from the ExAC and gnomAD databases and was classified as likely pathogenic. GABRB1 was among 9 genes newly implicated in EIMFS.

paragraphs.text: Janve et al. (2016) suggested that the faster rise time and slower deactivation caused by the GABRB1 F246S mutation would lengthen the first inhibitory postsynaptic current (IPSC) but reduce charge transfer during later IPSCs. The result would be a net loss of GABAergic inhibition. They suggested GABRB1 as a candidate human epilepsy gene.

paragraphs.text: Burgess et al. (2019) identified a de novo heterozygous missense variant in the GABRB1 gene in a patient with epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures (patient 63). The variant (Chr4:47405633T-C) results in an ile247-to-thr (I247T) substitution and was found by whole-exome sequencing. The patient had onset of focal seizures at 4 months of age, profound to severe developmental impairment, and hypotonia. The variant was absent from the ExAC and gnomAD databases and was classified as likely pathogenic.
